simple.meaning: פָּצָה (pâtsâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to rend , i.e. open (especially the mouth).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 15 times across Genesis, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Judges, Job, and 4 more, beginning at Genesis 4:11. Its contexts include family, family line, blood, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פָּצָה (H6475).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: פָּצָה (pâtsâh) / H6475 is traced through Genesis 4:11, Numbers 16:30, Deuteronomy 11:6, Judges 11:35 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: Now you are cursed because of the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.

But if Yahweh makes a new thing, and the ground opens its mouth, and swallows them up with all that belong to them, and they go down alive into Sheol,* Sheol is the place of the dead. then you shall understand that these men have despised Yahweh.”

and what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, the son of Reuben—how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up, with their households, their tents, and every living thing that followed them, in the middle of all Israel;
When he saw her, he tore his clothes, and said, “Alas, my daughter! You have brought me very low, and you are one of those who trouble me; for I have opened my mouth to Yahweh, and I can’t go back.”

She said to him, “My father, you have opened your mouth to Yahweh; do to me according to that which has proceeded out of your mouth, because Yahweh has taken vengeance for you on your enemies, even on the children of Ammon.”
Therefore Job opens his mouth with empty talk,
I am poured out like water.
Stretch out your hand from above,
You are he who gives salvation to kings,
Rescue me, and deliver me out of the hands of foreigners,

My hand has found the riches of the peoples like a nest, and like one gathers eggs that are abandoned, I have gathered all the earth. There was no one who moved their wing, or that opened their mouth, or chirped.”
All your enemies have opened their mouth wide against you.
“All our enemies have opened their mouth wide against us.
But you, son of man, hear what I tell you. Don’t be rebellious like that rebellious house. Open your mouth, and eat that which I give you.”

definitions.short: to rend , i.e. open (especially the mouth)
definitions.full: H6475. patsah [ מָּצָה ] verb part, open (Arabic I, II. separate, remove ; Aramaic מְּצָא especially set free , Pa`el set free ); — Qal Perfect 3feminine singular מָּֽצְתָה Gen 4:11 +, 2 masculine singular מָּצִיתָ Judg 11:36 , etc.; Imperfect 3masculine singular יִפְצֶה Job 35:16 ; Imperative masculine singular מְּצֶה Ezek 2:8 , suffix פְצֵנִי Psa 144:7 ; 144:11 ; Participle מֹּצֶה Isa 10:14 , ׳מּוֺ Psa 144:10 ; — 1 open mouth: a. to swallow, figurative of ground , הָאֲדָמָה Gen 4:11 , (J), Num 16:30 (JE), הָאָרֶץ Deut 11:6 ; of enemies, + עַל person Lam 2:16 ; 3:46 ; Psa 22:14 ; literal Ezek 2:8 . b. to speak Judg 11:35-36 , (utter a vow, + ׳אֶליֿ ); Job 35:16 ; hence = utter , שְׁפָתַי מָּצוּ אֲשֶׁר Psa 66:14 ; of bird chirping פֶה מֹּצֶה Isa 10:14 (in figurative). 2 snatch away, set free (Aramaic loan-word), only Psalm 144, + הִצִּיל with מִן Isa 10:7 ; 10:11 ; ׳פ with מִן 10:10 .
